issues.failure_explanation: The definition $F(x)=\mathbb{P}[X<x]$ is left-continuous with $F(0)=0$ and $F(1)=1-\mathbb{P}[X=1]$; the asserted right-continuity, $F(0)=\mathbb{P}[X=0]$ and $F(1)=1$ are properties of $x\mapsto\mathbb{P}[X\le x]$, so the recalled framework is internally incompatible, and the identity $\mathbb{E}[g(X)]=\int g\,dF$ fails at atoms for the strict CDF (e.g. $g=\mathbf{1}_{\{x_0\}}$ with $\mathbb{P}[X=x_0]>0$). Boundary conventions also disagree: Algorithm 2 branches on $c_n>r_n$ while the map $T$ and the definition of $\ell$ use $c\ge r$, and the proof of thm - pdf uses strict events $\mathbb{P}[\ell<t]$. For atomic cuts and an atomic prior with coinciding atoms these define different processes: with $r_0\equiv 1/3$ and cuts $\equiv 1/3$, Algorithm 2 gives $\ell_1=2/3, r_1=0$, whereas (eq - iteration_root)/(def - l) give $\ell_1=1/3, r_1=1$. Values of the displayed distribution functions at atom points (e.g. $H(t)$ at $t$ an atom of $c$) are convention-dependent.

failure_location.quote: Recall that any real-valued random variable $X$ on $[0,1]$ is characterized by its cumulative distribution function (CDF) $F(x)=\mathbb{P}(X< x)$, which is nonnegative, nondecreasing, right-continuous, and satisfy $F(0)=\mathbb{P}[X=0]$ and $F(1)=1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adopt one convention consistently (e.g. the standard CDF $\mathbb{P}[X\le x]$ with $dF$ equal to the law), correct the recalled properties, harmonize the $c\ge r$ versus $c_n>r_n$ conventions, and re-check the boundary bookkeeping in the Stieltjes computations (boundary events are null whenever $r_n$ or $c_n$ is non-atomic).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised unified Lebesgue--Stieltjes treatment of continuous, discrete and mixed distributions is unreliable at atoms: the recalled CDF properties are false as stated, the analyzed process is ambiguous when cuts and root have coinciding atoms, and boundary values of the displayed CDF formulas depend on an unstated convention. Substantive conclusions for non-atomic variables are unaffected.
issues.title: Internally inconsistent CDF/Stieltjes and boundary conventions break the advertised atom-level (discrete/mixed) generality
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local harmonization of conventions; the paper's substantive results concern non-atomic cases or quantities insensitive to boundary values, so every claim, rate and scope survives.

issues.failure_explanation: From $0\le c(1-c)\le\frac14$ one gets $0\le\mathbb{E}[c(1-c)]\le\frac14$, so the displayed inequality $\frac12\le\mathbb{E}[c(1-c)]\le 1$ is false (e.g. $c\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)$ gives $\mathbb{E}[c(1-c)]=1/6$). The intended quantity is $\mu_\ell=1-2\mathbb{E}[c(1-c)]\in[1/2,1]$, as the stated equality conditions confirm; the inference 'taking expectations thus yields' is invalid as written, and this display is the sole quantitative justification of cor:added-1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed quantity by $1-2\mathbb{E}[c(1-c)]$ (i.e. $\mathbb{E}[\ell_n]$) and derive $\frac12\le\mathbb{E}[\ell_n]\le 1$ from $0\le\mathbb{E}[c(1-c)]\le\frac14$ via the identity.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative argument supporting cor:added-1 (optimality of the classical bisection method) rests on a false displayed inequality as written; the corollary's conclusion itself is correct once the display is repaired.
issues.title: False displayed bound $\frac12\le\mathbb{E}[c(1-c)]\le 1$ in the justification of the optimality corollary

issues.failure_explanation: Part (ii) states only pairwise independence, and the written induction never re-establishes its hypothesis at step $n+1$ (nothing shows $r_{n+1}$ is independent of $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_{n+1}$); read pairwise, the hypothesis also cannot yield independence of $\ell_{n+1}$ from the vector $(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_n)$, which is what the proof's conclusion ('independent from $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_n$') asserts. The proof of cor:added-2 then factors $\mathbb{E}[\prod_{i=1}^n\ell_i]$ into a product of expectations, which requires mutual independence of all $\ell_i$ — never established in the source (pairwise independence does not suffice for $n\ge3$). The mutual independence is in fact true and follows by strengthening the induction to the joint law of $(r_n,\ell_1,\dots,\ell_n)$, reusing the paper's own computation of the joint law of $(r_{n+1},\ell_{n+1})$.

failure_location.quote: Assume that $r_n$ is independent from $\ell_i$ ($i=1,\dots,n$). The base case is validated by the computations above. $\ell_{n+1}$ depends only upon $r_n$ and $c_n$ in its construction. $c_n$ is clearly independent from all $\ell_i$. By the induction hypothesis, we can say the same about $r_n$. Thus, $\ell_{n+1}$ is independent from $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_n$ for all $n>0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen thm - ind(ii) to mutual independence and prove by induction that the law of $(r_n,\ell_1,\dots,\ell_n)$ equals $\mathcal{U}(0,1)\otimes H^{\otimes n}$, using the already-computed factorization of the law of $(r_{n+1},\ell_{n+1})$; cor:added-2 then follows verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The identity $\mathbb{E}[L_n]=\mathbb{E}[\ell_1]^n$ for the expected interval length after $n$ iterations — a headline convergence-rate formula of Section 2 — is unsupported as proven.
issues.title: Independence of the $\ell_n$: the induction yields at most pairwise independence, while $\mathbb{E}[L_n]=\mathbb{E}[\ell_1]^n$ requires mutual independence
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local strengthening of the existing induction that reuses the paper's own computation; every claim, rate and advertised scope survives.

issues.failure_explanation: First, the proof invokes thm - conv, which requires $\mathcal{T}$ to be a positive operator on $X=B_\circ[0,1]$; the paper only verifies $0\le(\mathcal{T}G)(t)\le 1$ for nondecreasing $G$ (CDFs) and then asserts positivity on all of $B_\circ[0,1]$ — a non sequitur. Positivity in fact fails for many admissible cut distributions: for $F=\delta_{1/2}$ (or any $F$ with density vanishing at the endpoints, e.g. Beta(2,2)) and a nonnegative bump $G$ supported near $1/2$, $(\mathcal{T}G)(1/2)=G(1/4)+G(3/4)-G(1/2)<0$. (For atomic $F$, the endpoint-continuity verification that $\mathcal{T}$ maps $B_\circ[0,1]$ into itself also breaks when $G_0$ has atoms coinciding with atoms of $F$, since $G(t+(1-t)c)\to G(c^+)\ne G(c)$.) Second, the statement itself is false: with cuts $c_n\equiv 1/2$ a.s. (allowed: not a.s. at 0 or 1) and $r_0\equiv 1/3$ a.s. (allowed: no mass at 0 or 1), $r_{n+1}=T(1/2,r_n)$ is the doubling map, $r_n$ cycles $1/3,2/3,1/3,\dots$, so $\mathcal{T}^kG_0$ alternates between the CDFs of $\delta_{1/3}$ and $\delta_{2/3}$ and does not converge to $t$ (sup-norm distance $2/3$); the displayed quantitative rate bound fails likewise. The digression's claim that the hypotheses are 'optimal' is therefore wrong: deterministic interior cuts must be excluded, and the Gavrea--Ivan route cannot prove the theorem for most remaining admissible $F$ (e.g. Beta(2,2) cuts used in the paper's own experiments), where positivity fails.

issues.failure_explanation: By thm - root_conv and the subsequent Remark, the convergence rate $1-2(\mu-\mu^2-\sigma^2)$ is determined by the CUT distribution. The Kolmogorov--Smirnov experiment is described with uniform cuts, for which the theoretical rate is $2/3$ for every initial root distribution $\mathcal{R}$; yet the 'Theoretical' row lists $1-2(\mu_{\mathcal{R}}-\mu_{\mathcal{R}}^2-\sigma_{\mathcal{R}}^2)$ computed from each initial root distribution (0.6, 0.7714…, 0.9385…, 0.5083…). Either the protocol (uniform cuts) or the benchmark is wrong; as written, the comparison against 'the upper bound given by the theorem' is false. In addition, the sentence 'The initial root distribution is always $\mathcal{U}(0,1)$, so $\mu_{\ell_n}\to 2/3$' contradicts the stated protocol (initial roots drawn from $\mathcal{R}$) and misidentifies the reason for the limit (the cuts are uniform, giving $\mu_\ell=2/3$); if the initial root were uniform, $|\mu_{\ell_n}-\mu_\ell|$ would be identically zero and the measured decay could not exist.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Determine and state the cut distribution actually used: either correct the protocol (cuts drawn from $\mathcal{R}$, which makes the Theoretical row the theorem's rates and matches the reported decay), or correct the Theoretical row to $2/3$ in every column and rewrite the narrative comparisons; also correct the false sentence about the initial root distribution.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical validation of the convergence-rate claims for non-uniform priors (tab:convrate, the surrounding narrative, and the conclusion's statement that the theoretical rates 'appear conservative' and that slower convergence is driven by asymmetry of $\mathcal{R}$) is unreliable as described.
